description: Approves the 2025 Annual Report for city council.

chips.text: Approved
Report includes suggested areas for future committee considerations.

description: Addresses snow removal, washrooms, website, and transit accessibility.
Incorporates feedback from 538 residents.
New provincial accessibility standards expected next year.

chips.text: Received as information
Councillor highlighted urgent need for snow removal and gender-neutral washrooms.
Engagement included blind, Indigenous, racialized communities, and older adults.
The multi-year plan is meant to be reviewed and updated every three years.
The actual implementation plan for accessibility initiatives is still being developed.
Plan aims for a more inclusive Saskatchewan for people with disabilities and older adults.
City staff committed to providing regular updates on the plan's implementation.

segments.title: Staff Presentation on Multi-Year Accessibility Plan
description: City consultant presented the new accessibility plan.
Plan aims for inclusive Saskatchewan for people with disabilities.
Focuses on identifying, removing, and preventing barriers.
Covers seven domains: built environment, information, transportation, service animals, city services, employment, and attitudes.

chips.text: Plan aims for inclusive Saskatchewan for people with disabilities and older adults.
City consultant will quickly review the plan and answer questions.

segments.title: Resident Input and Common Barriers
description: 538 residents engaged through surveys to share barriers.
Diverse groups, including blind, Indigenous, racialized, and older adults, participated.
Five common barriers identified: snow/ice removal, pedestrian infrastructure, public washrooms, outdoor spaces, and information access.

chips.text: 538 residents shared barriers and discussed removal strategies.
Engagement included blind, Indigenous, racialized communities, and older adults.

segments.title: Built Environment: Indoor and Outdoor Spaces
description: Residents face barriers in indoor navigation, doors, elevators, seating, and washrooms.
City actions include audits, design standards, barrier removal, and staff training.
Outdoor barriers include sidewalk ramps, snow clearing, surface conditions, and park access.
City plans to improve snow clearing, sidewalk repairs, signage, and park accessibility.

chips.text: Barriers affect people using mobility devices, deaf, hard of hearing, and those needing rest areas.
City plans audits, design standards, staff training, and improved snow clearing.

segments.title: Information and Communication Accessibility
description: Residents reported digital exclusion, website navigation issues, and document accessibility problems.
Staff lack training for diverse communication needs.
City plans include smart city AI, website upgrades, inclusive staff support, and multiple communication formats.

chips.text: Older adults and screen reader users face digital exclusion and navigation issues.
City plans AI for digital accessibility and website upgrades for better user experience.

segments.title: Transportation Accessibility
description: Residents reported issues with parking, narrow paths, accessible taxis, and transit services.
Bus stops lack clear information and audio cues for blind users.
City plans include redesigning bus networks, audible announcements, and electronic displays.
Improvements to Access Transit, sidewalks, curb ramps, and accessible signals are planned.

chips.text: Blind users lack audio cues; Access Transit services are complicated for users.
City plans to improve Access Transit with more vehicles and online booking.

segments.title: Service Animal Accommodations
description: Residents faced barriers with staff understanding and unclear policies.
People using service animals felt unwelcome in public spaces.
City plans to elevate staff understanding and create clear policies.
City departments will collaborate to uphold laws and provide accommodations.

chips.text: Service animal users felt unwelcome and unsupported due to staff knowledge gaps.
City plans to increase staff knowledge and create clear policies for service animals.

segments.title: City Services and Programs Accessibility
description: Residents reported complexity in registration, limited communication, and staff training gaps.
Leisure program sign-ups were unclear, and inclusive options were limited.
City plans include accessible services, policy clarity, and improved program access.
Purchasing policy will be updated to include accessibility as a core principle.

chips.text: Residents faced barriers with leisure program sign-ups and limited inclusive options.
City plans to update purchasing policy to make accessibility a core principle.

segments.title: Employment Accessibility
description: Residents found job application processes and information unclear.
Job seekers needed more accommodations and support for service animals.
City plans inclusive job postings and collaborative hiring practices.
Fair employment opportunities and clear language in applications are planned.

chips.text: People with disabilities faced barriers in job applications and accommodations.
City plans inclusive job postings and collaborative hiring to support people with disabilities.

segments.title: Attitudes and Biases in the Workplace
description: Residents reported staff assumptions, feeling unwelcome, and lack of understanding.
Invisible disabilities were not taken seriously, and negative attitudes created barriers.
City plans focus on respect, inclusion, training, and updating policies.
ASL, disability awareness, and accessible technology training are offered.

chips.text: People with invisible disabilities faced disbelief and disrespect from staff.
City plans training in ASL, disability awareness, and accessible technology.

segments.title: Questions and Answers on the Accessibility Plan
description: The multi-year plan covers three years, with a new plan every three years.
City website accessibility will use new technologies like AI for searchability.
Public washroom upgrades will prioritize existing ones based on community feedback.
Community surveys were distributed via posters, emails, and disability organizations.

chips.text: City will conduct new surveys every three years to update the accessibility plan.
Provincial deadline for the accessibility plan is December 3.

segments.title: Committee Discussion and Feedback
description: Committee member highlighted snow and ice removal as an urgent concern.
Expressed concern about lack of gender-neutral washrooms at City Hall.
Staff confirmed provincial regulations and standards are coming early next year.
Committee wants updates on implementation of top five accessibility items.

chips.text: Committee member emphasized snow and ice removal as an urgent concern for wheelchair users.
Lack of gender-neutral washrooms and wheelchair access at City Hall was highlighted.
Staff will provide regular updates to the committee on implementation plans.

segments.title: Motion to Send Letter of Support to Council
description: Committee considered options: feedback to SPC, letter of support, or receive as information.
A motion was made to send a letter of support to council.
The motion carried.

chips.text: Motion to send a letter of support to council carried.
